slate.name: The Slant Light
slate.why: We each tell one truth at a slant, and the whole panel is the single low light that falls across the room and shows every design its true shape.

slate.name: Pressed Hours
slate.why: A flower is pressed one at a time and kept true, and this panel presses each decision through its long night hours until only the essential shape remains.

slate.name: A Herbarium of Nights
slate.why: The herbarium is the old way of keeping every small thing true, and this panel is one such book, each guardian pressed flat and labeled, shown plainly to anyone who opens it.

slate.name: Quiet Walls
slate.why: A good gallery is remembered for its quiet walls, and this panel should step back the same way so that the painting is the first thing the eye finds.

slate.name: Courtyard Lanterns
slate.why: Elene Akhvlediani's Tbilisi courtyards each keep one small lantern lit so the street stays quiet, and this panel should keep its own light low enough that the painting, not the panel, is what the eye meets.

slate.name: The Picture Light
slate.why: A gallery's picture light falls on one painting and nothing else, and this name does the same job for the panel, lighting the picture and leaving the chrome in the dark.

slate.name: Clear Vigil
slate.why: A watch kept through the night is a vigil, and glass is the clearest thing to keep one with: the chrome stays quiet, the panel stays out of the way, and the painting is what shows.

slate.name: Stone and Glass
slate.why: Tbilisi's glass bridge stands over the old stone of the town, and that meeting of modern clarity and old craft is the work this panel does on every design.

slate.name: The Glass Choir
slate.why: Each guardian is one clear voice and glass rings when it is struck, so the panel is heard in one chord as well as seen.

slate.name: The Night Ballet
slate.why: A ballet is a dance that is seen and heard at once, and the guardians who work by night move together as one body, so the name asks the panel to be judged as a dance and not as a list of opinions.

slate.name: Pulse and Line
slate.why: Musicality and clean line are what I ask of every design, and this name keeps the count you can hear and the edge you can follow, which is all a panel of eighteen needs to stay in step.

slate.name: The Round Dance
slate.why: A round dance is the oldest way a people moves as one, each dancer keeping their place in the ring and the circle carrying them, and that is how these eighteen judge, with no one stepping out ahead.
